raw_case_text:
A 34-year-old previously healthy male presented with high grade fever associated with constitutional symptoms of five days' duration. He was complaining of right hypochondrium pain and tea-coloured urine for two days associated with yellowish discolouration of the eyes. He had severe loss of appetite to food and water, but his bowel habits had been normal throughout the illness. On admission, he was afebrile with normal vital signs but was deeply icteric. His abdominal examination revealed a tender, mild hepatomegaly while his cardiovascular, respiratory, and nervous system examination was normal.
His full blood count revealed a white cell count of 3 x 103 muL with a platelet count of 116 x 103 muL. His aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) were 5162 U/L and 3964 U/L, respectively. Initial total bilirubin was found to be 61.7 mumol/L with an increased direct fraction. His prothrombin time/international normalized ratio (PT/INR) and serum protein were normal throughout the illness. His dengue IgM antibody done by chromatographic immunoassay was positive on the 6th day of the illness. Hepatitis A IgM antibody done by the ELISA technique was positive on day 6 of the illness, while hepatitis A IgG antibody was negative. Other investigations done during the hospital stay are summarized in Table 1.
During the course of the illness, the patient was closely monitored for features of development of liver failure while continuing with the precritical monitoring of the dengue fever. The patient's hospital stay was uneventful, and he did not develop features of acute liver failure or features of plasma leakage as in DHF. He was discharged on day 10 of the illness. On follow-up, his AST, ALT, and bilirubin have become normal.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old male presenting with a 5-day history of high-grade fever, constitutional symptoms, right hypochondrial pain, tea-colored urine, and deep jaundice.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 34-year-old previously healthy male presented with high-grade fever and constitutional symptoms of 5 days' duration. Two days prior to presentation, he developed right hypochondrial abdominal pain, dark tea-colored urine, yellowish scleral discoloration, and severe anorexia to both solids and liquids. Bowel habits remained normal throughout.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy with no chronic medical conditions or known liver diseases.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, malaise, right upper quadrant pain, dark urine, jaundice, and severe anorexia. Negative for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or bleeding manifestations. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile, vital signs normal. Deeply icteric. Abdomen: Tender mild hepatomegaly. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological examinations were completely normal.
objective.routine_investigations: White blood cell count: 3 x 10^3/muL, platelet count: 116 x 10^3/muL. Liver biochemistry: AST 5,162 U/L, ALT 3,964 U/L, total bilirubin 61.7 mumol/L (with elevated direct bilirubin fraction). Coagulation and synthetic function: PT/INR and serum total protein/albumin remained normal throughout illness.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute co-infection of Dengue fever and acute Hepatitis A virus (HAV) presenting with marked acute transaminitis and cholestatic jaundice without acute liver failure or plasma leakage. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus IgM antibody by chromatographic immunoassay on illness day 6; positive Hepatitis A IgM antibody by ELISA on day 6 (Hepatitis A IgG antibody negative).
Plan & Outcome: Monitored closely for acute liver failure and plasma leakage while undergoing supportive dengue care and fluid management. Hospital course remained uneventful without coagulopathy or bleeding; discharged on day 10. Complete normalization of AST, ALT, and bilirubin documented on follow-up.
